comparisonFindings.finding: The anthology already teaches GA 327 lectures 4–6 extensively. The full books add a continuous lecture/discussion sequence and fresh source locators; these six lessons need source remapping and stronger full-discussion integration, not an invented replacement doctrine.
Creeger 74 and 75; Adams 87 and 88 repeatedly say the preparations enhance ordinary manuring. This must remain prominent.
Creeger 68,73 and Adams 80,86 explicitly leave measures to investigation and request figures/tables. Preserve the difference between confident spiritual claims and unfinished technical quantities.
Hand stirring favored spiritually (Creeger 66–67/Adams 78–79), fine mechanical spraying accepted (70/83), farm machinery generally accepted (71/83). No general machine ban.
Horn burial: Creeger 63 says 3/4–1 1/2 m [2 1/2–5 feet]; Adams 75 says 18 in.–2 ft.6 in. Preserve difference and avoid a course recipe. No PDF image check available.
Adams 77 labels 500/501 and 502–507 as editorial/current terminology and declines adding later technicalities to the lecture. These numbers are useful but not Steiner’s spoken numbering.
Creeger 74 says acids in moorland; Adams 86 says oxygen. Record OCR/translation discrepancy without silently correcting quoted source.

Teach plants, animal enclosure where named, seasonal exposure and attributed relationship. Nettle has no animal casing and whole-year burial; valerian is flower extract. Full Q&As distinguish separate burial from later addition to manure.
Quercus robur, outer living bark, Urtica dioica, nettle aerial flowering parts without roots; mesentery/peritoneum is not tripe; botanical substitution replies are tentative.

Food-substance through senses, microbes as only indicators, potash/lime to nitrogen alchemy, silicon unnamed element, metallic cosmic substances, disease prevention and insect/star effects are Steiner’s assertions. Do not present as established mechanisms or field prescriptions.

Growth preparations also support weeds (Creeger 87/Adams 102). Lecture 6 treats suppression separately and asserts four-year effects. Experiments invited but spiritual truth viewed as intrinsically certain (97/112–113), not left wholly conditional.
Nematodes are put with insects/lower animals by the speaker; this is historical grouping, not current zoology. Species and larval/adult timing still require testing.
Creeger 108 uses cabbage clubroot; Adams 123 cabbage root-fly. Distinct conditions; do not merge the translation into a single modern diagnosis.

Creeger 98 favors shared understanding with neighbors;106–107 audience misuse question and moral improvement circle are substantive. Vineyards explicitly untested(108/Adams 123), and ordinary proven methods retained(109/124).
The two translations witness the same 1924 GA 327 lecture sequence, not separate Agriculture courses.
